messages:
tom_sales: VerityCare sent back their security questionnaire for Private deployment. Asking: PrivateLink vs peering, static egress for allowlisting, firewall rules (including FQDNs), TLS inspection implications, and if we support Azure Private Endpoint. Need a short, clear pack.

rachel_neteng: Quick guidance: Prefer PrivateLink / interface endpoints for AWS and Private Endpoint for Azure for POC. Rationale: limits routing exposure, easier SG-level restrictions, and fewer long-lived peering objects to manage. For Azure, customer must create a private endpoint in their vnet and approve delegation; we do not create NICs in their subscription by default.

ari_solutions: Static egress options: 1) Customer-owned NAT/EIP (recommended) so they keep allowlist control. 2) Redwood-provided reserved egress IPs (add-on, provisioning lead time). For Azure, equivalent is a NAT gateway + public IPs. For short POC, ask customer to provide EIPs/PIPs.

sam_sec: TLS inspect: we dont perform in-platform MITM. If VerityCare performs TLS inspection, flag cert pinning issues for some SDKs and mobile apps. Recommend customer-side forward proxy. Note: any request to terminate TLS on Redwood systems requires legal/compliance approval. Also mention KMS/HSM controls for private deployments if they want BYOK.

rachel_neteng: Firewall / allowlist snippet to share:
```
Inbound to customer VPC (from Redwood PrivateLink / peering):
- TCP 443 to endpoint IPs (API traffic)
- TCP 443 for health checks (LB) if used
- UDP 123 NTP optional
- ICMP optional for diagnostics
If FQDN allowlist is required, provide these hostnames: api.redwood-inference.net, metrics.redwood-inference.net (note customers should prefer IP allowlist for PrivateLink).
```

ari_solutions: DDoS note: customers should use their cloud provider (e.g., Azure DDoS Protection or AWS Shield). We offer rate-limiting and request throttles but not third-party scrubbing.

deploy-bot: Provision log: test connector created (connector-706, us-east-1) 2026-02-12T09:02:11Z.

tom_sales: Action items: @rachel_neteng create a 1-page connectivity diagram (AWS+Azure variants) + allowlist template. @sam_sec prepare the TLS inspect blurb for the questionnaire. @ari_solutions draft short SOW line for reserved egress with lead time.

rachel_neteng: Will deliver diagram + CIDR guidance by EOD.

sam_sec: I'll add the compliance note and BYOK mention.

ari_solutions: I'll add prorated POC pricing for 2 IPs and note ~3-7 business day provisioning on Redwood side if requested.

tom_sales: Perfect, sending to VerityCare once docs are in. Any other blockers?

rachel_neteng: Only blocker would be if they insist Redwood creates NICs in their Azure subscription; that requires extra onboarding.

tom_sales: Noted. Closing thread for now :white_check_mark:
